text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate (gateway) and tail latencies observed in us-east-1 starting ~2026-03-15T03:12Z. 5xx spike at ingress gateway + downstream KV cache timeouts. Auto-detect: 5xx rate = 3.8% (5m), tail p95 latency = 980ms. Triggered pager to oncall. Metrics: https://dash.redwood/internal/gw-us-east?range=15m

mike: I'm on pager. grabbing context. Any active deploys or config changes in us-east in last hour?

anya: I see a big uptick in cache evictions on the edgepool: kv-cache eviction_count spiked from ~200/min -> 12k/min starting 03:12Z. Also seeing a correlated increase in backend connection timeouts to ml-workers.

sam: we did roll a config tweak to the prefix-invalidation job earlier that reduced batch size, but there was also a change to edgepool kv max-size (2GB -> 512MB) to test memory headroom. suspect combined effect.

infra-sre: logs show repeated prefix invalidation events from the job:
```
[03:12:07Z] prefix_invalidate: job=prefix-cleanup id=pr-441 keys_invalidated=14290 duration=320ms
[03:12:07Z] kvcache: evict triggered by mem-pressure used=97% limit=512MB
```
This caused thrashing and increased tail latency for requests that rely on prefix KV hits.

mike: ok. immediate ask: can we reduce traffic to us-east by shifting some percent to eu-west for a quick mitigation? what's the risk on cross-region auth/session affinity?

sam: session affinity is sticky by default for short requests, but long streaming chats may break if we cross-region. We should route non-streaming and short-gen traffic first.

incident-bot: routing-change suggested: shift 25% non-streaming traffic away from us-east -> eu-west to reduce pressure. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-evict#mitigation

alice: CS update: we have 9 customer reports of failed requests; top impacted: AcmeCorp (prod), PaperTrail (staging). Errors are 502/504 during longer prompt chains. Customers are seeing intermittent responses.

support-lead: drafting status note. recommend immediate customer-facing message once we confirm mitigation progress.

mike: I'm going to perform a staged route change for non-streaming routes now. command: `augman route adjust --from us-east --to eu-west --percent 25 --filter non-streaming`

infra-sre: heads up: changing weights will trigger some connection churn. we'll monitor connection pools. also preparing a hotfix to increase kv-cache limit to 1.5GB on edgepool as a less-disruptive alternative, but that requires rolling restart of ~20 nodes (10-15 min).

sam: quick mitigation: enable model fallback for heavy long-context requests to quantized variant (gptq-16k) which uses less worker memory; `redwoodctl model route --from model:prod-large --to model:gptq-16k --percent 50 --filter long-context`

mike: route change executed. now: non-streaming -> eu-west +25%. Observing immediate drop in 5xx from 3.8% -> 2.1%. p95 latency down ~180ms.

anya: KV eviction rate still high but less downstream pressure. I can start the rolling increase to kv-cache limit on a staggered set to avoid simultaneous restarts. proposing 3 nodes at a time.

infra-sre: we also found the invalidation job had a bad regex that matched too broadly (PR #441). PR created to tighten matches: https://git.internal/redwood/prefix-cleanup/pull/441. If we can pause the job temporarily, that will immediately reduce evictions.

sam: pausing job now. `kubectl patch cronjob prefix-cleanup -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'`

incident-bot: Cronjob prefix-cleanup suspended by sam at 03:26Z.

alice: CS: sent interim note to impacted customers: short blurb + we are mitigating by shifting traffic and pausing cleanup job. link to status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/1770012345

mike: ramped route shift to 40% (non-streaming) -> eu-west. 5xx now 0.9% overall. Tail latency p95 ~420ms. Noting a single OOM on node edgepool-12 during restart; investigating crash logs.

anya: OOM stack: `rss > limit` while handling a large prefix list during eviction. Looks like some large keys are being touched repeatedly. We're quarantining that node and bringing up replacement.

sam: PR #441 merged. will roll out fix to invalidation job after we validate the patch in staging.

eng-pm: proposed next steps: 1) keep routing shift in place for 30m monitoring 2) complete kv-cache limit bump with staggered restarts 3) roll out invalidation-fix and re-enable job on controlled schedule 4) postmortem to follow.

support-lead: recommend customer comms update after 30m if metrics hold. prepping language now.

infra-sre: started staggered kv limit bump (3 nodes at a time). so far 6/20 done, no further OOMs. eviction rate trending down.

mike: monitoring window: 15m stable. I'll keep oncall until we hand back. If metrics regress, we'll revert route to 75% us-east.

incident-bot: incident status: MITIGATED -> traffic diverted + job paused + kv limit bump in progress. Severity downgraded from P1 -> P2 at 03:45Z.

alice: CS: updated customers with mitigation summary and ETA for full resolution (config fix + re-enable job).

sam: final note: root cause appears to be combined effect of (a) aggressive kv-cache size reduction, and (b) a broad invalidation regex in the cleanup job. change to one alone might have been fine; together they caused eviction thrash. PRs: #441, #442 (kv limit rollback).

mike: handing off to infra-sre for monitoring and postmortem. I'll file the incident ticket and notify leadership. thanks all for quick response.

eng-pm: filing postmortem and action items: add guardrails for cronjob regex changes, add canary check for kv-limit config flips, and a playbook step to pause invalidation job automatically if eviction > 1k/min.

support-lead: closing customer comms loop after final note.

mike: incident thread closed; follow-up ticket: INT-2026-477 created for postmortem and action items. If anyone finds residual errors, re-open thread. Thanks. :thumbsup:
